title: Observable authorization log curation and evidence playbook
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary
This playbook prescribes a repeatable, audit-ready workflow for curating authorization (authz) and authentication (authn) logs into compliance evidence bundles. It covers log schemas, residency-aware retention, secure SDLC touchpoints, incident-response collection, and exception handling for risk-team approvals. The goal is to ensure every access decision that matters for compliance is observable, tamper-resistant, and packaged for audits within defined SLOs.

Scope
- Systems: API gateway, edge auth proxy, identity provider (IdP) assertions, service mesh, RBAC enforcement point, policy-evaluation service, admin consoles.
- Evidence types: authz decisions, token issuance/refresh, entitlement changes, role bindings, privileged session start/stop, delegation events.
- Audiences: security ops, compliance, SRE, product infra teams, legal.

Key definitions
- Decision Log: canonical record for an access decision (allow/deny) with context.
- Proof Bundle: cryptographically verifiable archive containing log slice, policy snapshot, role-mapping, and ingestion metadata for a given incident or audit window.
- Residency Boundary: geographic / legal boundary determining where PII or customer data can be stored.

Principles
- Always-on observability: authz telemetry must be emitted synchronously at enforcement points.
- Minimal latency impact: logs may be buffered, but not dropped; buffer thresholds ensure SLOs for request latency are met.
- Immutable tagging: each decision log gets an immutable trace_id, signing_key_id, and ingestion_timestamp.
- Residency-aware packaging: proof bundles must only include data allowed by the residency boundary of the tenant/customer.

Roles and responsibilities
- Security (owner): defines evidence format, signing policy, retention class, and approves exceptions.
- SRE/Platform: implements collectors, retention enforcement, and backup.
- Product Infra: maintains policy snapshot tooling and rollout linkage.
- Compliance: accepts proof bundles and performs audit completeness checks.

Logging requirements (schema and constraints)
Provide the canonical event schema for any enforcement point. All fields are required unless marked optional.

| field_name | type | required | example | notes |
|------------|------|----------|---------|-------|
| trace_id | string | required | tx-4f9b3c | UUID or span-id tying request traces to logs |
| timestamp_iso8601 | string | required | 2026-01-30T14:23:02Z | ingest client must use UTC |
| decision | string | required | allow/deny | canonical boolean as string |
| principal_id | string | required | user:alice@example.com | subject that requested access |
| principal_type | string | required | user/service | helps filter PII for residency |
| resource | string | required | model-serving:inference:request | resource identifier |
| action | string | required | generate/rollback/read | action attempted |
| policy_version | string | required | policy:v2026-01-28-4 | snapshot id of policy used |
| reason | string | optional | rate_limit_disabled | policy decision explanation |
| token_hash | string | optional | sha256(...) | hashed token id (masked in some regions) |
| enforcement_point | string | required | edge-auth-proxy | hostname/service |
| signing_key_id | string | required | sig-2026-01 | key used to sign this record |

Retention and residency model
- Retention classes: short-term (30 days), medium (1 year), long-term (7 years). Mapping to class is defined by classification rules in the retention registry.
- Residency constraints: tenant residency label appended to each decision log. Bundles for cross-border incidents must follow the cross-region-review procedure prior to movement.
- Automatic purging: SRE runs a monthly enforcement job that verifies retention policy and triggers secure deletion flows.

Secure SDLC integration
- Policy snapshotting: every policy change merges into a policy repository (git) and uses a deterministic snapshot id. The deploy pipeline records the policy_version tag and embeds it into the policy_version field in decision logs.
- Pre-merge checks: changes to RBAC or policy evaluation code require: unit tests, policy-consistency lint, static analysis for PII exfil patterns, and a security review label.
- Release gate: production rollout requires evidence bundle generation tests in staging that demonstrate log emission and proof-bundle creation for a sample workload.

Incident response collection procedure (quick play)
1) Triage and scope: incident lead identifies affected residency and initiates an evidence-capture ticket.
2) Freeze window: if live systems may overwrite logs, apply a short-term snapshot retention extension for impacted services (actioned by SRE on approval).
3) Collect proof bundle: follow the Proof Bundle checklist (below).
4) Verify integrity: check bundle manifests and signature verification using the signing_key_id key.
5) Handoff and storage: upload to the evidence vault (region-bound) and notify Compliance and Legal.

Proof Bundle checklist (must be included)
- Decision log slice (ndjson) covering the incident period.
- Policy snapshot (policy repo commit + human-readable rendered policy).
- Role mapping snapshot (current RBAC bindings).
- Service deployment manifest (image tags, config hash).
- Signing manifest: signatures of the decision log slice and manifest.json, with signing_key_id metadata.
- Chain-of-custody record: who requested/assembled the bundle, timestamps, and approvals.

Evidence packaging rules by residency
- For tenants in EU residency, PII fields (principal_id) are pseudonymized in shared audit extracts; full principal_id included only in proof bundles stored in EU vault.
- For US tenants, include masked token identifiers in audit extracts; full token_hash allowed in proof bundle when stored in US vault.
- For cross-border lawful requests, follow legal & compliance approval workflow (see "Risk exceptions and cross-border flow" below).

Risk exceptions and approval process
- Exceptions may be requested when operational constraints prevent meeting the logging or residency requirements (e.g., 3rd-party SaaS forwarder without regional storage).
- Exception request must include: impact statement, proposed compensating controls, TTL (max 90 days), and rollback plan.
- Approvers: Security (primary), Legal (if cross-border), Compliance (if audit scope affected).
- Exception automation: approved exceptions are recorded in the exception registry with a scheduled automated expiration and reminder to reviewers.

Operational playbook: daily and monthly tasks
Daily:
- Verify collector health dashboards: ingestion lag < 30s across 99th percentile.
- Random bundle smoke-test: assemble a 1-hour proof bundle from staging and verify signatures.
Monthly:
- Retention enforcement run and deletion audit report.
- Key rotation check: verify signing_key_id rotation has been reflected in manifests.
- Cross-team tabletop: run a 30-min evidence handoff drill with Compliance and SRE.

Sample CLI snippets
- Assemble a proof bundle (example):
  redwood-evidence assemble --service edge-auth-proxy --start 2026-01-30T14:00:00Z --end 2026-01-30T15:00:00Z --output /tmp/bundle-20260130.tar.gz

- Verify signatures:
  redwood-evidence verify /tmp/bundle-20260130.tar.gz --keystore /var/keys/signing-pubring.json

Audit readiness SLOs and metrics
- Time-to-bundle: 95% of incident proof bundles assembled and uploaded within 4 hours of request.
- Completeness: 99.9% of enforcement points include required fields in logs across the rolling 30-day window.
- Integrity: 100% of stored proof bundles pass signature verification during random sampling.

Appendix: common failure modes and mitigations
- Missing policy_version: detect in CI via policy-injection linter; block merges that would remove policy snapshoting.
- Clock skew: enforce NTP and validate timestamp drift during daily collector health checks.
- Over-redaction: compliance complaints from audit; provide a reversible pseudonymization service that keeps a sealed mapping inside the regional vault.
